source: How to fill a weekly pill organizer (made-up example)
original:
HOW TO FILL YOUR WEEKLY PILL ORGANIZER
Use a pill organizer with 7 days and 2 times per day (AM and PM).
1. Pick one day each week to fill it, for example Sunday. 2. Wash and dry your hands. 3. Line up your pill bottles and your medication list. 4. Fill one medicine at a time: put it in every box where it belongs, then put the bottle away. 5. When you finish, compare each box with your medication list. 6. Close all the lids.
Do not put liquid medicines, inhalers, or pills that must stay in their package into the organizer.
If a pill is a different color or shape than usual, call your pharmacy before taking it: (919) 555-0102.
Ask a family member or your pharmacist to check your organizer the first few times.

source: How to check your blood pressure at home (made-up example)
original:
HOW TO CHECK YOUR BLOOD PRESSURE AT HOME
Before: Do not smoke, exercise, or drink coffee for 30 minutes. Empty your bladder.
Steps: 1. Sit in a chair with your back supported and both feet flat on the floor. 2. Rest quietly for 5 minutes. 3. Put the cuff on your bare upper arm, at heart level, on the arm your doctor told you to use. 4. Press start. Do not talk or move. 5. Write down both numbers and the time. 6. Wait 1 minute and take a second reading.
Your goal: below 130/80. Bring your log to every visit.
Call your doctor at (919) 555-0123 if your top number is above 180 or your bottom number is above 110 on two readings.
Call 911 if your blood pressure is that high AND you have chest pain, trouble speaking, weakness, or vision changes.

ROUTINE EEG (ELECTROENCEPHALOGRAM) — PATIENT INSTRUCTIONS
An EEG records the electrical activity of your brain using small metal discs (electrodes) placed on your scalp with a paste. It does not hurt and does not send electricity into your body.
Appointment: Monday, February 22, 2027 at 1:00 p.m., Neurology Testing, Westfield Medical Plaza, 600 Oakmont Drive, Suite 310.
The night before: wash your hair with shampoo only. Do not use conditioner, oil, gel, or hairspray. Your doctor may ask you to sleep less than usual the night before; follow the instructions on your order.
Take your usual medications unless your doctor tells you otherwise. Avoid caffeine on the day of the test.
The test takes about 60 to 90 minutes. You may be asked to breathe deeply and look at a flashing light.
To reschedule: (919) 555-0103.

lines.text: Small **metal discs** go on your **head** with a **paste**.
It does **not** put **electricity** into your body.
Your doctor may ask you to **sleep less**.
You may look at a **flashing light**.
